issues.legal_issue: Agricultural produce derived from land through agricultural operations and used in the grower’s own business constitutes agricultural income even when it is not sold.
material_facts: The company grew bamboos, thatching grass, and fuel timber on leased land through agricultural operations carried out by its servants and labourers.
It used the produce in its tea business and did not sell it.
The tax authorities included the produce’s market value in the company’s agricultural income.
issues.conclusion: The produce used in the company’s own business constituted agricultural income; a sale or receipt of money from a sale was not required.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(1)(b)(i) of the Bengal Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1944, includes income derived from land by agriculture, and its plain wording includes agricultural produce used by the grower. The contrast with clauses (ii) and (iii), which address processes making produce marketable and income from sales, supports that reading; section 7(1) likewise corresponds to the three clauses. The Court considered Alexander Tennant v. Robert Sinclair Smith and In re Micklethwait on clear words of taxation, and Sir Kikabhai Premchand v. Commissioner of Income-tax on a person not trading with himself, but found them unhelpful because agricultural income need not be profit or gain from a sale. Commissioner of Income-tax v. Shaw Wallace & Co. and Captain Maharaj Kumar Gopal Saran Singh v. Commissioner of Income-tax were not applicable to the issue; the meaning of income depends on the relevant taxing provision and may include a receipt that is not a profit.

rule.if: agricultural_income_tax_assessment and produce_grown_by_agricultural_operations and produce_used_in_own_business and not produce_sold

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns whether receipts or produce are taxable as agricultural income.
predicates.produce_grown_by_agricultural_operations: The grower produced the agricultural goods on land through agricultural operations.
predicates.produce_used_in_own_business: The grower used the agricultural goods in its own business.
predicates.produce_sold: The grower sold the agricultural goods.
predicates.produce_constitutes_agricultural_income: The agricultural goods constitute agricultural income.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns agricultural-income taxation and the grower produces goods through agricultural operations, uses them in its own business, and does not sell them, the goods constitute agricultural income.

issues.legal_issue: Agricultural produce that is not sold in the market can have its value computed under the residual valuation method for agricultural-income assessment.
material_facts: The company used the bamboos, thatching grass, and fuel timber it grew in its tea business rather than selling them in the market.
The assessment included a value for that produce, and the company argued that no rule permitted its computation.
Rule 4(1) addressed produce sold in the market, while Rule 4(2) set out a method for produce not sold in the market.
issues.conclusion: Rule 4(2) applies to produce sold outside the market and to produce not sold at all, so the produce’s value could be computed under that rule.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 4(1) of the rules under the Bengal Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1944, applies to produce sold in the market. Rule 4(2) is the residual rule for cases not covered by Rule 4(1), including produce sold outside the market and produce not sold at all. The Court noted that the rules were made under section 57 and could not be used to construe the Act itself.

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns the assessment of agricultural income.
predicates.produce_not_sold_in_market: The grower did not sell the agricultural produce in the market, whether or not it was sold elsewhere.
predicates.produce_value_computable_under_residual_: The produce’s value can be computed under the method applicable to produce not sold in the market.

issues.definition: In an agricultural-income assessment, produce not sold in the market can have its value computed under the residual method.
